axes.label: Origin
axes.description: How the data came to exist — the mechanism of its production.

values.label: Sensor
values.description: Produced by a physical measurement device: cameras, microphones, accelerometers, biosensors. The world writes the data directly.

values.label: Exhaust
values.description: A byproduct of activity, not intentionally recorded as data. Transaction logs, metadata, DNS queries, click streams. The data exists because a system ran, not because anyone chose to capture it.

values.label: Declared
values.description: Someone chose to submit it. Surveys, registries, self-reports, administrative filings. The data reflects what people or institutions say, not what they do.

values.label: Derived
values.description: Produced by processing other datasets. Model outputs, aggregates, inferences, synthetic data. The data is downstream of other data.

axes.label: Status
axes.description: The current condition of the dataset — whether it is accessible, hidden, lost, or not yet real.

values.label: Active
values.description: Being generated and held now. Access may be restricted, but the data exists and is current.

values.label: Buried
values.description: Exists but is inaccessible — controlled by a gatekeeper, suppressed, classified, or locked behind proprietary systems. The data is real; reaching it is the problem.

values.label: Missing
values.description: Should exist but doesn't. No one collected it, or collection was never mandated. The absence is a choice, often a political one.

values.label: Emerging
values.description: Newly possible — a dataset that couldn't exist before due to technology, regulation, or scale, and is now beginning to be generated.

values.label: Eroding
values.description: Exists now but is being lost: short retention windows, discontinued sensors, decaying physical records, deliberate deletion. The window to capture it is closing.

axes.label: Scale
axes.description: The unit of resolution — what one record in the dataset describes.

values.label: Individual
values.description: One record = one person, one body, one device carried by a person. The data can identify or profile a specific human being.

values.label: Organizational
values.description: One record = one company, institution, vehicle, or other non-human entity. Aggregated above the person, below the population.

values.label: Systemic
values.description: One record = a city, a market, a network, a policy domain. The data describes how a system behaves, not any single actor within it.

values.label: Planetary
values.description: One record = a global or environmental measurement. Climate, ocean, atmosphere, species. The subject is Earth or a major system of it.
